rounds.text: HRS Aluglaze trades at a significant premium with a P/E of 48.8 and a P/B of 6.55, which is nearly triple the sector benchmark of 2.44 [E1, E2, E7]. This rich valuation leaves a negative margin of safety of -117.1%, as the current market price of Rs 256 far exceeds the DCF-derived intrinsic value of Rs 118 [E31, E30]. Despite reporting profits, the company suffers from poor cash conversion of -1.10x and negative free cash flow of Rs -35 Cr, exacerbated by working capital days ballooning from 45.6 to 117 [E19, E21, E36]. Institutional confidence appears to be waning, with domestic institutions slashing their holdings from 8.13% to 2.71% and foreign institutions also reducing their stake [E28, E27]. Conceded: The company has demonstrated strong trailing twelve-month profit growth of 97% and maintains a healthy ROE of 21.35% [E15, E9]. However, the current price implies a 20.7% earnings growth rate—more than double the base case assumption—while operating margins remain inconsistent [E32, E17].
